result:
Both integrate one branch into another. Difference is history shape.

**`git merge`**: joins two branches with a new merge commit. Existing commits unchanged. History keeps the fork, shows when branches joined. Safe on shared branches.

**`git rebase`**: replays your commits on top of the target branch. Creates new commits with new hashes. History becomes linear, no merge commit. Rewrites history.

```
Before:        A---B---C  main
                    \
                     D---E  feature

merge:         A---B---C---M  main
                    \     /
                     D---E

rebase:        A---B---C---D'---E'  feature
```

Conflicts: merge resolves once. Rebase may ask per replayed commit.

Never rebase commits others already pulled. Their history diverges from yours, and fixing it needs a force-push that can overwrite their work.

Use rebase to tidy a local feature branch before sharing. Use merge to bring finished work into a shared branch.
